title: Got $5,000? 2 Growth Stocks Building the Software Backbone of the AI Revolution
author: Leo Sun
description: The article highlights Amazon and Palantir as two AI software companies positioned to benefit from the AI market's rapid expansion. Amazon's AWS provides cloud infrastructure and AI services like Bedrock and SageMaker, with additional upside from its Anthropic stake. Palantir offers data aggregation platforms (Gotham and Foundry) that enable AI application development. Both companies are expected to deliver strong revenue and earnings growth through 2028, though Palantir trades at a premium valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AWS is positioned as a linchpin of the AI market with strong growth prospects. The company benefits from Anthropic stake, expected 15% revenue CAGR and 24% EPS CAGR through 2028, and reasonable valuation at 25x forward earnings.

Palantir's data aggregation and AI integration capabilities position it as a key player in the AI revolution. Expected 58% revenue CAGR and 70% EPS CAGR through 2028 demonstrate strong growth, though premium valuation at 87x forward earnings is noted as a consideration.
Mentioned as a popular AI chipmaker focus, but the article positions software companies as underappreciated alternatives rather than endorsing or criticizing Nvidia.

title: Better Global ETF: Vanguard's VT vs. the iShares URTH
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Vanguard's Total World Stock ETF (VT) is recommended over iShares MSCI World ETF (URTH) due to its significantly lower expense ratio (0.06% vs 0.24%), broader global diversification including emerging markets, higher dividend yield (1.8% vs 1.4%), and larger asset base. While both offer similar sector allocations and comparable performance, VT provides exposure to key AI-related companies like TSMC and SK Hynix that URTH excludes.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better choice due to lower expense ratio (0.06%), higher dividend yield (1.8%), broader diversification with 9,773 holdings including emerging markets, larger AUM ($101.7B), and exposure to key AI semiconductor companies like TSMC and SK Hynix.

Presented as a viable alternative but with notable limitations: higher expense ratio (0.24%), smaller portfolio (1,253 holdings), developed markets only, lower dividend yield (1.4%), and lacks exposure to emerging market AI-related companies. Performance is comparable but cost structure is less favorable.

title: Invest Like Buffett: Lessons From the Oracle of Omaha
author: Na
description: Following Warren Buffett's step down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, the article explores his investment philosophy emphasizing long-term ownership, high-quality businesses with economic moats, and low-cost index funds. Buffett's approach has delivered nearly double the S&P 500's returns over six decades. The article highlights his preference for index funds over active management, focus on companies with durable competitive advantages, and recent increased investments in Japanese trading houses.

title: Zapata Introduces Quantum Pilot™ to Enable Systematic Discovery and Development of High-Value Quantum Applications
author: Zapata Quantum, Inc.
description: Zapata Quantum announced early access to Quantum Pilot, a hardware-agnostic cloud-based platform designed to help enterprises identify and develop quantum computing applications with commercial value. The platform combines proprietary knowledge frameworks with AI-powered tools developed through collaborations with NVIDIA and University of Maryland to provide Quantum Application Intelligence, addressing the gap between advancing quantum hardware and enterprise ability to determine practical business applications.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company announced a significant new product launch (Quantum Pilot) addressing a critical market gap, demonstrated strategic partnerships with NVIDIA and University of Maryland, received endorsement from industry leader CSL Behring, and has strong intellectual property portfolio (60+ patents). The platform positions the company as a leader in quantum application development with clear commercial focus.

NVIDIA is mentioned only as a collaboration partner for agentic AI capabilities in quantum resource estimation. The mention is factual and promotional in nature with no material business impact disclosed.

title: CrowdStrike vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: The article compares CrowdStrike and Palantir Technologies as investment options for 2026. CrowdStrike offers a leading cybersecurity platform with 22% revenue growth but remains unprofitable and faces reputational damage from a 2024 outage. Palantir demonstrates stronger financial performance with 56% revenue growth, profitability, and no debt, but carries higher valuation and customer concentration risks. The author recommends CrowdStrike for its better balance between growth and valuation, despite ongoing challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong market position and resilient stock recovery post-outage, but offset by ongoing unprofitability (-3.4% net margin), reputational damage from July 2024 incident, and slower growth (21.7% YoY). Recommended by author as better value despite challenges.

Exceptional financial performance with 56.2% revenue growth, strong profitability (36.3% net margin), zero debt, high liquidity, and expanding commercial customer base. However, positive sentiment is tempered by high valuation multiples and customer concentration risk.
